title: RSF Gives Conditional Response to US Peace Plan; Rejects Full Withdrawal
detail: The RSF submitted its response to the US peace plan on July 14, 2026, agreeing 'in principle' to an unconditional three-month humanitarian truce with UN-supervised aid access to Darfur, Kordofan, Blue Nile, and the Nuba Mountains, but rejecting full or gradual withdrawal from territory it holds, especially in North Darfur and North Kordofan. US envoy Massad Boulos cautioned against declaring a breakthrough. Combined with SAF's July 10 demand for full RSF withdrawal as a precondition, both sides gave incompatible conditional responses — no ceasefire was reached. The same day, SAF's 4th Infantry Division claimed recapture of Fashfoun, Blue Nile State, from RSF/SPLM-N as a follow-on to the Kurmuk operation (moderate confidence — reported by mid-tier outlets, not independently corroborated by wire services).

title: WFP Warns 5 Million Face Emergency Hunger; EU Bans Sudanese Gold Imports
detail: The World Food Programme warned on July 14, 2026 that approximately 5 million Sudanese face emergency or catastrophic hunger (IPC Phase 4-5), with 100,000+ still in Phase 5 famine-like conditions and 19.5 million acutely food insecure overall. WFP said its caseload was cut from 5 million to 3.5 million beneficiaries due to a $646 million funding shortfall, and that aid delivery to El Obeid was capped at 100,000 of a 250,000-person target despite a brief lull in fighting that opened an aid window; renewed fighting closed the Tine border crossing in Darfur the same period. Separately, the EU announced a ban on Sudanese gold imports on July 14, citing conflict-financing concerns — gold being the RSF's principal war-financing mechanism, with an estimated 55+ tons smuggled 2023-2025, roughly 70% via the UAE.
